Kate Ramakaieva

Excited to be hunting Navige today!   
  
What caught my attention is how simple the idea is: most of what AI agents do doesn't need the most expensive model, but that's usually what runs every single call. Navige gives each task just the model it needs, only ever moves calls down, and falls back to your original model if a smaller one fumbles. Plus budgets, approval holds and a kill switch for when an agent goes off the rails.   
  
What I love most is Watchtower, which is free forever and just shows you what it would save before you switch anything on. Congrats @sojimathewj and the team on the launch! Let's go!

Report

Soji Joseph

Navige

Maker [...] Navige sits in front of calls routed through it and acts before they run, while the cost can still change. We call this Sufficiency Intelligence: give each task exactly the intelligence it needs.

How it works

1. It assesses each request and sends suitable ones to a smaller model. Your model is the ceiling: Navige only moves calls down, never up, and keeps yours whenever it’s unsure.
2. If the smaller model fumbles a tool call, the call re-runs on your original model, and your agent only sees that answer.
3. It records every job: what it cost, what the controls changed and what made the difference. Measured savings and estimates are clearly separated.

On top of that, you get budgets per team and per job, approval holds for risky actions, a kill switch and an audit trail.

results.content:
Report

Tina Chhabra

BetterClaw

the "run agents like a company" framing makes sense because that's where things are heading. one agent is easy, five agents doing different things across different workflows gets chaotic fast. curious how you handle cost visibility though... like if one agent starts looping and burning through tokens, is there a way to set per-agent spending limits or kill switches before the bill surprises you

Report

Kazim Akgül

AgentOS

Maker

@tina\_chhabra Exactly — this is one of the core problems we’re trying to solve with AgentOS.

OpenClaw is powerful, and our goal is to make it more manageable, transparent, and accountable for real operations. [...] Today, every agent already has visibility around which model it uses, task/session activity, token usage, and task-level execution details. From there, the natural next layer is operator controls: per-agent budgets, task-level cost tracking, spend alerts, loop detection, and kill switches before anything gets out of hand.

So yes — the goal is not just “run more agents.”

It’s to make agent work visible, measurable, and controllable.

Report

Zaid Mallik

Once multiple agents share a workspace, coordination seems to become more important than raw model capability.

Are users spending more effort defining agent roles, or managing the shared context between them?

Report

Kazim Akgül

AgentOS

Maker [...] We're building something in the AI workflow space and have found that reducing coordination overhead often creates bigger gains than improving the individual agents themselves. Looking forward to seeing how AgentOS evolves this.
